title: After-Timeout (ATO) Set Play
description: Coming out of a timeout, the team runs a specifically called set play designed to get a clean look for the team's best shooter.

content.objective: Execute a called set play cleanly right out of a timeout to generate a good shot for the primary target.
content.setup: Five players set up in the called formation as if coming straight out of a timeout.
instructions: Each player sets up in their exact spot for the called play before the inbound or first action.
Run the designed screening and cutting sequence exactly as called.
The primary target reads the defense and takes the shot if open, or passes to the backup option.
Reset and run the same play again to build repetition and timing.
coachingPoints: Know your exact role and spot before the play begins — there's no time to figure it out live.
Set screens with real conviction since this is a one-shot opportunity.
Have a clear backup option if the primary read is covered.
commonMistakes: Players unsure of their spot or role, breaking the timing of the play.
Forcing the primary option even when the defense has taken it away.
Rushing the set instead of trusting the timing of the play.
content.safety: Screens must be legal and stationary; keep the simulated play at game-realistic intensity.
